title: Rupin Pass Trek
reportingPoint: Dehradun. The exact meeting point and reporting time are shared once your booking is confirmed. The trek ends at Sangla on Day 8.
highlights: Views of the Kinnaur Kailash range from the pass
Rupin waterfall views from the Saruwas Thatch campsite
Trail from Dhaula through Sewa, Jhaka and Dhanderas Thatch to Sangla
Camping, vegetarian meals, permits, trekking equipment and a certified trek leader
overview:
Rupin Pass is a mountain pass in Himachal Pradesh at around 15,250 ft, and the trek to it starts from Dhaula in Uttarakhand and finishes at Sangla. This **7 Nights / 8 Days** trek is graded easy to moderate. It starts from Dehradun: you need to reach Dehradun on your own on Day 1 and travel on to Dhaula for the first night at the campsite.

Day 2 is the 7 km trek from Dhaula to Sewa (6,300 ft) and Day 3 the 9 km trek to Jhaka (8,700 ft). Days 4 to 6 climb through Saruwas Thatch (11,150 ft) and Dhanderas Thatch (11,680 ft) to the Upper Waterfall camp (13,120 ft). Day 7 crosses Rupin Pass (15,250 ft) and descends to Ronti Gad, a 10 km day of about 11 hours. Day 8 is the 12 km descent to Sangla, where the trek ends. Camping, vegetarian meals on the trek, permits, trekking equipment and a trek leader are included. Batches run from May to September, with daily departures. Prices start at ₹16,499 per person (5% GST extra); dual sharing accommodation costs ₹1,000 extra per person.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Dehradun | Dehradun to Dhaula
itinerary.content:
Arrive in Dehradun, for example by train from Delhi.
Travel from Dehradun to Dhaula. One option is a bus from Dehradun to Naitwar, followed by a shared jeep ride to Dhaula village.
Overnight stay at the campsite in Dhaula.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dhaula to Sewa
itinerary.content:
Altitude: 6,300 ft. Trek duration: 7 hours. Trek distance: 7 km.
The trek starts from a point just outside Dhaula.
Pass a few villages along the trail; after a while the Rupin River comes into view, flowing through a canyon about 500 ft below.
Walk along the left side of the valley, past apple and apricot trees.
Stop at a small shop on the way for tea and light snacks.
Reach Sewa, a village a short distance above the bed of the Rupin River, with a small temple in the Kinnauri style.
Continue along the trail to the stream near the village.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sewa to Jhaka
itinerary.content:
Altitude: 8,700 ft. Trek duration: 7 hours. Trek distance: 9 km.
Walk along crop fields in the morning and enter the forest.
Reach a wooden bridge known as "No Man's Place" because it belongs to no state.
Continue to Gosangu and on towards Kwar: cross the river on a bridge and take the track that leads up to the village.
From Kwar, join the steeply climbing trail to Jiksun village, along the right bank of the river.
After another hour of walking, reach Jhaka village and camp for the night.

itinerary.title: Trek from Jhaka to Saruwas Thatch
itinerary.content:
Altitude: 11,150 ft. Trek duration: 5 hours. Trek distance: 6 km.
The trail descends at first and becomes steeper and more difficult as it approaches a tributary of the main river.
Walk through the forest to a snowfield.
Follow the snow bridge into a rhododendron forest.
A few more kilometres of walking bring you to the Saruwas Thatch campsite.
Overnight at the campsite, with views of the Rupin waterfall.

itinerary.title: Trek from Saruwas Thatch to Dhanderas Thatch
itinerary.content:
Altitude: 11,680 ft. Trek duration: 4 hours. Trek distance: 5 km.
Walk through maple and blue pine forest in the morning.
Cross the bridge over the river to move from the right side of the valley to the left.
The maple forest gives way to silver birch and rhododendron, and then to alpine meadows.
In the blooming season the meadows have wild flowers and blue poppies.
Reach the campsite for the overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Dhanderas Thatch to Upper Waterfall camp
itinerary.content:
Altitude: 13,120 ft. Trek duration: 2-3 hours.
Set out for the Upper Waterfall camp after acclimatising at Dhanderas.
Cross patches of snow and fields of marigold flowers to reach a snow trail.
After a short but steep ascent, reach the campsite and rest for the night.

itinerary.title: Upper Waterfall camp to Ronti Gad via Rupin Pass
itinerary.content:
Altitude: 15,250 ft. Trek duration: 11 hours. Trek distance: 10 km.
The trail gets narrower and steeper, and this is a harder day than the earlier ones.
The route passes through boulder sections; if there is snow on the ground, a rope is used for support.
Reach Rupin Pass, with views of the Kinnaur Kailash range.
Descend to the alpine meadows and camp overnight at Ronti Gad.

itinerary.title: Ronti Gad to Sangla via Sangla Kanda
itinerary.content:
Altitude: 8,800 ft. Trek duration: 6 hours. Trek distance: 12 km.
Descend towards Sangla, with views of the Sangla Valley.
The trail gets steeper as it drops towards Sangla, so walk carefully and at a comfortable pace.
About an hour and a half of downhill walking brings a drop of more than 1,500 ft.
The trek ends on reaching Sangla.
From Sangla you can stay on in the town or travel onwards to Shimla.

faqs.q: Where does the trek start and end?
faqs.a: The trek starts from Dehradun on Day 1, with the first night at the campsite in Dhaula, and ends at Sangla on Day 8. You travel to Dehradun yourself, for example by train from Delhi, and go on to Dhaula from there; one option is a bus from Dehradun to Naitwar, followed by a shared jeep ride to Dhaula village. The exact meeting point and reporting time are shared once your booking is confirmed.

faqs.q: How much does the Rupin Pass Trek cost?
faqs.a: ₹16,499 per person. Dual sharing accommodation is ₹1,000 extra per person, which makes it ₹17,499. 5% GST is extra.

faqs.q: How difficult is the trek and how high does it go?
faqs.a: The trek is graded easy to moderate. The highest point is Rupin Pass at 15,250 ft, crossed on Day 7, which is a 10 km day of about 11 hours on a narrower, steeper trail.

faqs.q: How much trekking is there each day?
faqs.a: Day 2 is 7 km (7 hours) to Sewa, Day 3 is 9 km (7 hours) to Jhaka, Day 4 is 6 km (5 hours) to Saruwas Thatch, Day 5 is 5 km (4 hours) to Dhanderas Thatch, Day 6 is 2-3 hours to the Upper Waterfall camp, Day 7 is 10 km (11 hours) over Rupin Pass to Ronti Gad and Day 8 is 12 km (6 hours) down to Sangla.

Camping during the trek, vegetarian meals on the trek, a campfire where available, trekking permit and forest campsite fees, trekking equipment (tents, sleeping bags, ice axes, ropes), a certified trek leader, a trek crew, safety gear and a trek certificate of completion. Backpack offloading (₹300 per day per bag) and food on the way during the pick-up and drop journeys are not included.

faqs.q: What do I need to carry?
faqs.a: Non-skid, deep-treaded hiking shoes, lightweight slippers or sandals, track pants, full-sleeve T-shirts, rainwear, a sun cap, sunscreen and lip balm, a toiletries kit, dry fruits and chocolate bars, a power bank and your personal medicines. Carry a valid government-approved photo ID as well. The full list is under Things To Pack.

faqs.q: How do I book and pay?
faqs.a: Reserve your seat by paying 50% of the trip cost, and pay the rest at least 4 days before the trip. 5% GST is added to the price.

Cancel more than 10 days before the travel date and 50% of the advance is refunded; 5 to 10 days before, 25% of the advance; less than 5 days before, there is no refund. There is no refund for no-shows or early check-outs.
